headline: Large User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, including data centers, to bear more of the costs for increasing electric generating capacity and distribution infrastructure, aiming to prevent these costs from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration, consumer and environmental advocates, Senator Louise Lucas, Dominion Energy (with amendments), Electricity Customer Alliance.
opponents: Data Center Coalition (initially concerned about language), critics of Governor's amendments who felt they weakened the bill.
news_headline: Virginia Bill Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to High-Demand Users
news_summary: Virginia's HB 1393 directs the State Corporation Commission to establish rates that require large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity. This legislation aims to prevent these infrastructure costs from being passed on to residential customers, potentially saving them money on their utility bills.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water utilities to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, increasing transparency regarding their water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, community advocates, environmental groups like Potomac Conservancy, Chesapeake Bay Foundation.
opponents: Data center industry (initially, as they felt singled out, but also point to low overall water usage).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Be Public
news_summary: SB 553, sponsored by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, making this information publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency and inform public discourse on data center water consumption, which has been a growing concern.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities (HEUF) like data centers, requiring site assessments for sound profiles near residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Community advocates, Del. Josh Thomas, Faith Alliance for Climate Solutions.
opponents: Data center industry (generally, as restrictions can affect economic growth).
news_headline: Virginia Bill Introduces New Data Center Siting Requirements
news_summary: HB 153 introduces new siting requirements for large data centers, mandating impact assessments on sound profiles near homes and schools, and allowing localities to require assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites before rezoning approval. This legislation provides localities with more tools to manage data center development and address community concerns.
